quote: erhält [-...-] für $P$ eine Differentialgleichung 3ter Ordnung, deren Coefficienten wahrscheinlich nur vom 2ten oder 1sten Grade sind.
english: one obtains for $P$ a differential equation of third order whose coefficients are probably only of 2nd or 1st degree.
topic: Notes on using continued fraction (and ternary chain-algorithm) expansions of the error-type function $e^{x^2}\int_0^x e^{-t^2}dt$ together with $e^{-x^2}$ to prove irrationality results, via differential equations, recursion formulas and generating functions.

triage.modern_statement: Context: one forms simultaneous (Hermite–Padé type) rational approximations, by a ternary analogue of the continued-fraction algorithm, to the pair f(x)=e^{x^2}∫_0^x e^{-t^2}dt and g(x)=e^{-x^2}. P is presumably the generating function, or one of the approximating polynomial families, attached to this algorithm. The note conjectures that P satisfies a linear ODE of order 3 whose polynomial coefficients have degree at most 2, or possibly 1. That would give short recursions for the approximants and could lead to irrationality proofs for values of these functions. The page does not say exactly what P is (e.g. which index or normalization), so the claim cannot be pinned down as a precise statement.
triage.answered_by: I found no source that addresses this specific remark. The general method it belongs to, Hermite–Padé approximation used for irrationality proofs, later became standard. The underlying arithmetic question, about the nature of values of erf-type E-functions, was taken up by the Siegel–Shidlovskii theory of E-functions. That theory was not verified in this search and is not cited here.

evidence.claim: Hermite–Padé approximation (type I/II simultaneous rational approximation) is a standard method for proving irrationality, e.g. of ζ(2), ζ(3) and log values. This is the framework Hilbert's ternary chain-algorithm notes anticipate.

triage.why: The remark is a working guess, during a calculation, about the order and coefficient degrees of an ODE for an object P that the note does not define. It is a technical step, not a stated research problem, and it is not among Hilbert's published problems. One search found only general literature on Hermite–Padé approximation and irrationality, which is still an active field, but nothing that addresses this particular ODE claim. Without knowing exactly what P is, the claim cannot be checked against later literature.
